title: Do QUF and QIND-CCA2 Imply QAE?
summary: Classically, unforgeability with IND-CCA2 implies authenticated encryption; whether QUF and QIND-CCA2 imply QAE for quantum encryption remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Classically, unforgeability together with IND-CCA2 security implies authenticated encryption. Determine whether the analogous implication holds for quantum encryption: does $\mathrm{QUF} \land \mathrm{QIND\text{-}CCA2} \implies \mathrm{QAE}$ for every encryption scheme?

scope.domain: The problem concerns security-property implications for quantum encryption schemes, including quantum unforgeability, QIND-CCA2, and QAE.
parameters: QIND-CCA2, the quantum chosen-ciphertext security premise
QAE, the target quantum authenticated-encryption property
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether every quantum encryption scheme satisfying QUF and QIND-CCA2 security also satisfies QAE.

progress.summary: The paper lists this in its discussion among several open questions. It recalls that classical unforgeability and IND-CCA2 imply authenticated encryption, then asks whether QUF and QIND-CCA2 imply QAE in the quantum setting.
citation_labels: Gorjan Alagic et al., Unforgeable Quantum Encryption
